original_target.title: Polynomial mixing of planar Ising dynamics with plus boundary

full_original_statement:
Fix $`\beta>\beta_c^{(2)}=\frac12\log(1+\sqrt2)`$. On $`\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}^2`$ take Ising spins with all exterior spins fixed to $`+1`$ and Gibbs weight proportional to $`\exp(\beta\sum_{x\sim y}\sigma_x\sigma_y)`$, summing over edges meeting $`\Lambda_n`$. Run continuous-time heat-bath Glauber dynamics: each interior site, at rate one, resamples its spin from the Gibbs conditional law.

Let

```math
t_{\rm mix}(n,\beta)=\inf\{t:\max_\eta\|P_t(\eta,\cdot)-\mu_{n,\beta}^+\|_{\rm TV}\le1/4\}.
```

For every fixed $`\beta>\beta_c^{(2)}`$, do finite constants $`C_\beta,a_\beta`$ exist with $`t_{\rm mix}(n,\beta)\le C_\beta n^{a_\beta}`$ for all $`n\ge1`$?

sources.scope_comparison: The exact target is a polynomial worst-initial-state mixing bound for finite plus-boundary boxes at each fixed beta>beta_c. The current primary Theorem1 treats biased iid initializations on a torus/infinite lattice, not every finite-box start. Section1.2 explicitly identifies polynomial plus-boundary mixing as open and proves only a uniform-in-large-beta quasi-polynomial input in AppendixA. This does not replace exp((log n)^C) by n^a for all boxes. No full matching announcement was found.
